subject: stf
title: STF.------IST.S.ALGN.
description: Second diagram on page 465, paired with the IST-F × AFL-DY × AFI-1 triple-crossing above. Where the first diagram shows the three-axis exclusion-of-no-one route, this one closes by structurally showing where the artist's structural-form has to land if the political-creativity relationship the prose names is to hold: (C)STF (the central structural-formal phenomenon — the artist's working form) is crossed with IST-S-ALGN (isolated-source alignment — where the form would actually align if it were not isolated). STF sits at top-center with the subject-arrow; PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) hangs at upper-left and PROJ-CONT (projectional continuance) at upper-right as the form's two upward outputs — what the form is supposed to keep continuing. ALT-D (alternative definitions) drops at lower-left as the subject's downward output. CUL-TF-S (cultural-transfer-source) sits centrally below PROJ-CONT, with APP-RDEF (applied redefinitions) as the central downward hub. IST-F (isolated focus) hangs below APP-RDEF and IST-S-ALGN anchors the bottom-right as the partner-axis terminus. Structural argument: the prose declares 'the political implications of creativity can no longer be controlled by white people exclusively — especially the political implications of creative music from the black aesthetic.' Structurally that is the claim that APP-RDEF on the central bottom must *not* be the only path STF reaches IST-S-ALGN through. The diagonal from PROG-CONT down through ALT-D back to APP-RDEF is the route by which the form's own progressional-continuance can reach applied-redefinitions on the subject's terms; otherwise, CUL-TF-S routes directly from PROJ-CONT to APP-RDEF and the partner-axis's alignment is reached only through cultural-transfer (the very mechanism the prose says must no longer be controlled exclusively). The artist's structural-form aligns isolated-source only when alternative-definitions hold the diagonal; that is what the next-cycle responsibility actually requires.
